AmbDescription:
First 2026 Maryland Canicross Meetup!
MD Ambassador Marea Schulman
Sunday, May 10, 2026- 10:30 AM
Little Bennett Regional Park-Horse Trailer Parking Area
26029 Prescott Rd.
Clarksburg, Maryland. 
Little Bennett Regional Park is located in the northern part of Montgomery County, near the Frederick County border.  It is about 33 miles north of Baltimore.
We will be doing the Sidewinder Trail and Dark Branch Loop, which is approximately 4 miles in length.  This meetup is beginner friendly!  However, everyone should be aware of their own and their dog's physical and/or mental fitness level and call it, if those levels are reached before the loop is completed.  For those of you that leave the trail loop while there are still teams out on the trail, please wait for everyone to finish, at the parking lot, if at all possible.  We want to make sure that everyone is accounted for and has returned safely.  
Don't forget to bring water and snacks for you and your dog.  
If you are not a member of North American Canicross, you will need to fill out a waiver form. 
It would be nice to get feedback from those of you who plan on attending, so we can have an idea of how many participants to expect.
There will be a couple of different styles/brands of dog harnesses (large breed sizes only) for anyone who is looking, to try for size.  I also have 2 different styles of waistbelts for you to try as well.
We will be having meetups at different trails in the region.  Some will be closer to you than others.  We strive to pick parks that have interesting, spacious trails, which are well marked, with elevation and footing varieties and are at least 3 miles.  We will go to places that have water access for the dogs in warmer months.  All trails are canicross-approved footing (e.g. unpaved)

AmbDescription: Join Hendrick and I for a canicross run. This is one of the flattest, potentially fastest, and (arguably) most scenic 5K trail runs in Westchester. We're talking a whopping 94 feet of ascent over the duration with a lot of single track and technical bits that include dirt, mud, sand, and rock surfaces, with just enough root to keep one super focused. This is an out and back run and we will keep the pace appropriate to whomever shows to work on running with other canicrossers and overtaking/directional commands. The trail head parking lot is small, additional parking is available on the shoulder of the road. No admission or parking fees. Interested, though don't want to run with your dog yet, or are hoping to have a dog soon, feel free to show up and say hello or even better run along without a dog.

AmbDescription:
Join us for a **NACC Canicross Meetup on May 30, 2026** at the beautiful Market at Grelen—a stunning 1,000-acre tree nursery and event property known for its scenic views, orchards, and welcoming outdoor spaces. Nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Grelen offers a peaceful yet invigorating setting perfect for hitting the trails with your dog.

This meetup is open to **all fitness levels**, with **multiple trail options and distances** to choose from. The terrain ranges from **rolling hills and grassy paths to wooded trails and gravel roads**, giving both you and your dog a dynamic and engaging run or walk.

I’ll have a **harness try-on kit available**, so if you’re curious about proper canicross gear, you’ll be able to try different harnesses on your dog and test out **bungee leashes** before investing.

Please come prepared to:

- **Pick up after your dog**
- Keep your dog **on leash at all times**

Whether you're brand new to canicross or already hooked, this is a great opportunity to learn, connect, and enjoy the outdoors together.

For questions, please reach out to **[harnessCanicular@gmail.com](mailto:harnessCanicular@gmail.com)**.

AmbDescription: Join Hendrick and I for a 5K canicross trail run in beautiful Ward Pound Ridge Reservation. We will meet in the northwest corner of the Meadows Parking Lot. The run will be over varied terrain including grass, dirt, mud, some item 4, roots, rocks, and wooden bridges with moderate elevation change (for Westchester) on trials roughly following the Cross River upstream to the Kimberly Bridge parking area and then back, mix of wide and single track trails. Pace will be set to keep the group together and work on overtaking skills. The aim is to have fun, learn, and build the community not drop people. Remember the reservation does charge a daily access fee, see their website for particulars.
